text.p: These are leading stories in this morning's Paris newspapers.
-- President Jacques Chirac to give television interview tonight at 1950 GMT to explain his government's policies and define goals for the country. (Les Echos, La Tribune, Le Figaro)

-- Government announces decision to privatise Thomson SA in two stages -- first defence unit Thomson-CSF in early 1997, and then consumer electronics unit Thomson Multimedia after a recapitalisation. (Les Echos, La Tribune, Le Figaro, Liberation)
-- Carrefour retail group buys 33.34 percent of GMB, which controls hypermarkets Cora. (Les Echos, La Tribune, Le Figaro, Liberation)
-- Senate to look at bill introducing private pension funds in France amid controversy from unions who fear employers may divert wages into pension funds from mandatory retirement schemes.
-- PSA Peugeot Citroen carmaker chairman Jacques Calvet expects European car market to be flat in 1997, sees new car sales down 10 percent in France in 1997.
-- Construction sector expected to stagnate in 1997, could shed up to 30,000 jobs, industry ministry and professional association reports say.
-- German chemicals group Hoechst buys out minority stake in Roussel Uclaf for an estimated 18.5 billion francs.
-- Retiring white-collar workers' pensions to decrease by 10 to 20 percent over the next 10 years, study shows.

-- Arms manufacturer Giat Industries and ailing state-owned bank Credit Lyonnais to limit planned layoffs under terms of Robien law allowing a reduction in labour charges in exchange for reduced work schedules to save jobs.
-- Intermarche supermarkets group ordered by Paris court to reimburse agrifood suppliers from whom it had obtained unlawful price cuts.
-- Korean executives lash out at France over decision to postpone sale of Thomson Multimedia to Daewoo, hint at negative effects on trade.
